name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: WHO counts over 3,000 cholera deaths in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa; DR Congo, Sudan and Yemen hard hit
state: WHO said on 10 Nov that more than 3,000 people died of cholera from January to September 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa, fewer than in the same period of 2025, the deadliest year since 1999 (Rio Times; Ahram Online). ECDC's monthly overview to 28 Sep counts DR Congo as the worst affected, with 1,050 deaths, and lists Yemen and Afghanistan among countries with the most new deaths (ECDC). Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones keep the Alert, though the global toll is below last year's.
for_you: Travellers to affected areas should follow FCDO travel advice and NHS travel health guidance on safe water, food hygiene and cholera vaccination. Displaced people in conflict zones are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Alert: large cholera outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones (3,000+ deaths in 2026, WHO; DR Congo 1,050)

sources.title: Rio Times — WHO: cholera deaths in 2026, Africa and El Niño
Ahram Online — Cholera killed more than 3,000 this year: WHO

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
